The issue is actually really easy to understand. Everybody knows Newton's third law that states for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction, but that doesn't make too much intuitive sense on Earth. Instead imagine for instance you were in space inside a box (like a ship) at rest and you wanted to start moving. What would you do? Well one obvious idea is to throw something to get some movement started. So let's say you take a ball and apply a force of 10 'left' on it. This in turn results in that ball applying a force of 10 'right' on you (imagine throwing a basketball while on ice skates - you'd end up going backwards a little bit, but without friction+gravity you'd end up going going backwards indefinitely until you hit something and transferred your momentum to it). The problem is that you will both hit the edges of the box with you then transferring a force of 10 'right' on the right side, and the ball applying a force of 10 'left' on the left side. The momentums end up cancelling out. You're still standing still.

So how could you change your velocity? You open up one side of the box! Now you do the same thing but open up the left side of the box. Now the ball never hits the left side of the ship to cancel out the 10 'right' you've ended up transferring to the box by throwing the ball out. You've now generated thrust and the box is moving to the right!

This is the fundamental idea of the law of conservation of momentum. Momentum within closed systems (a system where nothing is going in or out, and no outside forces are acting on it) is conserved. In order to generate thrust you need to expel something. Exhaust from rocket engines is not an unfortunate side effect, it's what actually causes them to move! So now enter the EM drive, the whole reason it's physically controversial is because it's generating thrust without expelling anything which completely contradicts the law of the conservation of momentum which we have observed as being true in every single experiment, situation, and scenario ever.

Don't electric engines contradict this? No, an electric engine -Earth style- where you just have an electric engine causing a rotor to rotate would do nothing in space. On Earth, Earth is the entire closed system. Bodies within Earth are not closed since they have enormous forces acting upon them - gravity in particular. Without gravity you would not stay 'stuck' to earth and so turning your wheels would do nothing. In space when we use electric engines, like ion drives, they also have to expel something to generate momentum - typically xenon gas.
